audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Judges / Shoftim post-Joshua incomplete-conquest and settlement register, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for post-Joshua inquiry, Judah-Simeon alliance, Adoni-bezek mutilation, Jerusalem/Hebron/Debir traditions, Achsah's water request, Kenite settlement, forced-labor notices, and repeated non-dispossession formulas.

verses.restored: It was after death of Joshua that children of Israel asked YHWH, saying, Who shall go up for us first against Canaanite, to fight against him?

familiar.text: Now after the death of Joshua it came to pass, that the children of Israel asked the LORD, saying, Who shall go up for us against the Canaanites first, to fight against them?

modern.text: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites inquired of the LORD, “Who will be the first to go up and fight for us against the Canaanites?”

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה לָּ֧נוּ אֶל הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: YHWH said, Judah shall go up. Look, I have given land into his hand.

familiar.text: And the LORD said, Judah shall go up: behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.

modern.text: “Judah shall go up,” answered the LORD. “Indeed, I have delivered the land into their hands.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֣ה יַעֲלֶ֑ה הִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיָדֽוֹ

verses.restored: Judah said to Simeon his brother, Go up with me into my lot, and let us fight against Canaanite; I also will go with you into your lot. So Simeon went with him.

familiar.text: And Judah said unto Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot. So Simeon went with him.

modern.text: Then the men of Judah said to their brothers the Simeonites, “Come up with us to our allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. And we likewise will go with you to your territory.” So the Simeonites went with them.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְשִׁמְע֨וֹן אָחִ֜יו עֲלֵ֧ה אִתִּ֣י בְגוֹרָלִ֗י וְנִֽלָּחֲמָה֙ בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וְהָלַכְתִּ֧י גַם אֲנִ֛י אִתְּךָ֖ בְּגוֹרָלֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן

verses.restored: Judah went up, and YHWH gave Canaanite and Perizzite into their hand; they struck them at Bezek, ten thousand men.

familiar.text: And Judah went up; and the LORD delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand: and they slew of them in Bezek ten thousand men.

modern.text: When Judah attacked, the LORD delivered the Canaanites and Perizzites into their hands, and they struck down ten thousand men at Bezek.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת הַכְּנַעֲנִ֥י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֖י בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיַּכּ֣וּם בְּבֶ֔זֶק עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and struck Canaanite and Perizzite.

familiar.text: And they found Adonibezek in Bezek: and they fought against him, and they slew the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

modern.text: And there they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him, striking down the Canaanites and Perizzites.

original.text: וַֽ֠יִּמְצְאוּ אֶת אֲדֹנִ֥י בֶ֨זֶק֙ בְּבֶ֔זֶק וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ בּ֑וֹ וַיַּכּ֕וּ אֶת הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י וְאֶת הַפְּרִזִּֽי

verses.restored: Adoni-bezek fled, and they pursued after him, seized him, and cut off thumbs of his hands and big toes of his feet.

familiar.text: But Adonibezek fled; and they pursued after him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his great toes.

modern.text: As Adoni-bezek fled, they pursued him, seized him, and cut off his thumbs and big toes.

original.text: וַיָּ֨נָס֙ אֲדֹ֣נִי בֶ֔זֶק וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אַחֲרָ֑יו וַיֹּאחֲז֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ וַֽיְקַצְּצ֔וּ אֶת בְּהֹנ֥וֹת יָדָ֖יו וְרַגְלָֽיו

verses.restored: Adoni-bezek said, Seventy kings with thumbs of their hands and big toes of their feet cut off used to gather under my table; as I have done, so Divine has repaid me. They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

familiar.text: And Adonibezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their meat under my table: as I have done, so God hath requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.

modern.text: Then Adoni-bezek said, “Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off have gathered the scraps under my table. As I have done to them, so God has repaid me.” And they brought him to Jerusalem, where he died. The Capture of Jerusalem and Hebron (Joshua 15:13–19)

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹֽנִי בֶ֗זֶק שִׁבְעִ֣ים מְלָכִ֡ים בְּֽהֹנוֹת֩ יְדֵיהֶ֨ם וְרַגְלֵיהֶ֜ם מְקֻצָּצִ֗ים הָי֤וּ מְלַקְּטִים֙ תַּ֣חַת שֻׁלְחָנִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי כֵּ֥ן שִׁלַּם לִ֖י אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיְבִיאֻ֥הוּ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיָּ֥מָת שָֽׁם

verses.restored: Children of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it; they struck it by edge of sword and sent city into fire.

familiar.text: Now the children of Judah had fought against Jerusalem, and had taken it, and smitten it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.

modern.text: Then the men of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put the city to the sword and set it on fire.

original.text: וַיִּלָּחֲמ֤וּ בְנֵֽי יְהוּדָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ וַיַּכּ֖וּהָ לְפִי חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת הָעִ֖יר שִׁלְּח֥וּ בָאֵֽשׁ

verses.restored: Afterward children of Judah went down to fight against Canaanite dwelling in hill country, Negev, and Shephelah.

familiar.text: And afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites, that dwelt in the mountain, and in the south, and in the valley.

modern.text: Afterward, the men of Judah marched down to fight against the Canaanites living in the hill country, in the Negev, and in the foothills.

original.text: וְאַחַ֗ר יָֽרְדוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה לְהִלָּחֵ֖ם בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֑י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָהָ֔ר וְהַנֶּ֖גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָֽה

verses.restored: Judah went against Canaanite dwelling in Hebron; name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-arba. They struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

familiar.text: And Judah went against the Canaanites that dwelt in Hebron: (now the name of Hebron before was Kirjatharba:) and they slew Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai.

modern.text: Judah also marched against the Canaanites who were living in Hebron (formerly known as Kiriath-arba), and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה אֶל הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ הַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּחֶבְר֔וֹן וְשֵׁם חֶבְר֥וֹן לְפָנִ֖ים קִרְיַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֑ע וַיַּכּ֛וּ אֶת שֵׁשַׁ֥י וְאֶת אֲחִימַ֖ן וְאֶת תַּלְמָֽי

verses.restored: From there he went against inhabitants of Debir; name of Debir formerly was Kiriath-sepher.

familiar.text: And from thence he went against the inhabitants of Debir: and the name of Debir before was Kirjathsepher:

modern.text: From there they marched against the inhabitants of Debir (formerly known as Kiriath-sepher).

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֔ם אֶל יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י דְּבִ֑יר וְשֵׁם דְּבִ֥יר לְפָנִ֖ים קִרְיַת סֵֽפֶר

verses.restored: Caleb said, Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him Achsah my daughter as wife.

familiar.text: And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.

modern.text: And Caleb said, “To the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give my daughter Acsah in marriage.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר כָּלֵ֔ב אֲשֶׁר יַכֶּ֥ה אֶת קִרְיַת סֵ֖פֶר וּלְכָדָ֑הּ וְנָתַ֥תִּי ל֛וֹ אֶת עַכְסָ֥ה בִתִּ֖י לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, and he gave him Achsah his daughter as wife.

familiar.text: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.

modern.text: So Othniel son of Caleb’s younger brother Kenaz captured the city, and Caleb gave his daughter Acsah to him in marriage.

original.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּדָהּ֙ עָתְנִיאֵ֣ל בֶּן קְנַ֔ז אֲחִ֥י כָלֵ֖ב הַקָּטֹ֣ן מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וַיִּתֶּן ל֛וֹ אֶת עַכְסָ֥ה בִתּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: It was, when she came, that she urged him to ask from her father a field; she dismounted from donkey, and Caleb said to her, What is for you?

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when she came to him, that she moved him to ask of her father a field: and she lighted from off her ass; and Caleb said unto her, What wilt thou?

modern.text: One day Acsah came to Othniel and urged him to ask her father for a field. When she got off her donkey, Caleb asked her, “What do you desire?”

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗הּ וַתְּסִיתֵ֨הוּ֙ לִשְׁא֤וֹל מֵֽאֵת אָבִ֨יהָ֙ הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַתִּצְנַ֖ח מֵעַ֣ל הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַיֹּֽאמֶר לָ֥הּ כָּלֵ֖ב מַה לָּֽךְ

verses.restored: She said to him, Give me a blessing, for you have given me land of Negev; give me springs of water. Caleb gave her upper springs and lower springs.

familiar.text: And she said unto him, Give me a blessing: for thou hast given me a south land; give me also springs of water. And Caleb gave her the upper springs and the nether springs.

modern.text: “Give me a blessing,” she answered. “Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well.” So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר ל֜וֹ הָֽבָה לִּ֣י בְרָכָ֗ה כִּ֣י אֶ֤רֶץ הַנֶּ֨גֶב֙ נְתַתָּ֔נִי וְנָתַתָּ֥ה לִ֖י גֻּלֹּ֣ת מָ֑יִם וַיִּתֶּן לָ֣הּ כָּלֵ֗ב אֵ֚ת גֻּלֹּ֣ת עִלִּ֔ית וְאֵ֖ת גֻּלֹּ֥ת תַּחְתִּֽית

verses.restored: Children of Kenite, father-in-law of Moses, went up from city of palms with children of Judah into wilderness of Judah, which is in Negev of Arad; they went and dwelt with the people.

familiar.text: And the children of the Kenite, Moses’ father in law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which lieth in the south of Arad; and they went and dwelt among the people.

modern.text: Now the descendants of Moses’ father-in-law, the Kenite, went up with the men of Judah from the City of Palms to the Wilderness of Judah in the Negev near Arad. They went to live among the people.

original.text: וּבְנֵ֣י קֵינִי֩ חֹתֵ֨ן מֹשֶׁ֜ה עָל֨וּ מֵעִ֤יר הַתְּמָרִים֙ אֶת בְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְבַּ֣ר יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּנֶ֣גֶב עֲרָ֑ד וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אֶת הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck Canaanite dwelling in Zephath and devoted it to destruction; name of city was called Hormah/Devotion.

familiar.text: And Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they slew the Canaanites that inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. And the name of the city was called Hormah.

modern.text: Then the men of Judah went with their brothers the Simeonites, attacked the Canaanites living in Zephath, and devoted the city to destruction. So it was called Hormah.

original.text: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ יְהוּדָה֙ אֶת שִׁמְע֣וֹן אָחִ֔יו וַיַּכּ֕וּ אֶת הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יוֹשֵׁ֣ב צְפַ֑ת וַיַּחֲרִ֣ימוּ אוֹתָ֔הּ וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שֵׁם הָעִ֖יר חָרְמָֽה

verses.restored: Judah captured Gaza and its territory, Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.

familiar.text: Also Judah took Gaza with the coast thereof, and Askelon with the coast thereof, and Ekron with the coast thereof.

modern.text: And Judah also captured Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron—each with its territory.

original.text: וַיִּלְכֹּ֤ד יְהוּדָה֙ אֶת עַזָּ֣ה וְאֶת גְּבוּלָ֔הּ וְאֶֽת אַשְׁקְל֖וֹן וְאֶת גְּבוּלָ֑הּ וְאֶת עֶקְר֖וֹן וְאֶת גְּבוּלָֽהּ

verses.restored: YHWH was with Judah, and he dispossessed hill country, but he could not dispossess inhabitants of valley because they had chariots of iron.

familiar.text: And the LORD was with Judah; and he drave out the inhabitants of the mountain; but could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

modern.text: The LORD was with Judah, and they took possession of the hill country; but they could not drive out the inhabitants of the plains because they had chariots of iron.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֶתּ יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖רֶשׁ אֶת הָהָ֑ר כִּ֣י לֹ֤א לְהוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָעֵ֔מֶק כִּי רֶ֥כֶב בַּרְזֶ֖ל לָהֶֽם

verses.restored: They gave Hebron to Caleb as Moses spoke, and he dispossessed from there three sons of Anak.

familiar.text: And they gave Hebron unto Caleb, as Moses said: and he expelled thence the three sons of Anak.

modern.text: Just as Moses had promised, Judah gave Hebron to Caleb, who drove out the descendants of the three sons of Anak.

original.text: וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ לְכָלֵב֙ אֶת חֶבְר֔וֹן כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֣ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מִשָּׁ֔ם אֶת שְׁלֹשָׁ֖ה בְּנֵ֥י הָעֲנָֽק

verses.restored: But Jebusite dwelling in Jerusalem children of Benjamin did not dispossess; Jebusite dwells with children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.

familiar.text: And the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites that inhabited Jerusalem; but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem unto this day.

modern.text: The Benjamites, however, failed to drive out the Jebusites living in Jerusalem. So to this day the Jebusites live there among the Benjamites.

original.text: וְאֶת הַיְבוּסִי֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב יְרֽוּשָׁלִַ֔ם לֹ֥א הוֹרִ֖ישׁוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב הַיְבוּסִ֜י אֶת בְּנֵ֤י בִנְיָמִן֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: House of Joseph, they also went up to Bethel, and YHWH was with them.

familiar.text: And the house of Joseph, they also went up against Bethel: and the LORD was with them.

modern.text: The house of Joseph also attacked Bethel, and the LORD was with them.

original.text: וַיַּעֲל֧וּ בֵית יוֹסֵ֛ף גַּם הֵ֖ם בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמָּֽם

verses.restored: House of Joseph caused Bethel to be spied out; name of city formerly was Luz.

familiar.text: And the house of Joseph sent to descry Bethel. (Now the name of the city before was Luz.)

modern.text: They sent spies to Bethel (formerly known as Luz),

original.text: וַיָּתִ֥ירוּ בֵית יוֹסֵ֖ף בְּבֵֽית אֵ֑ל וְשֵׁם הָעִ֥יר לְפָנִ֖ים לֽוּז

verses.restored: Watchers saw a man going out from city, and they said to him, Show us, please, entrance of city, and we will do covenant loyalty with you.

familiar.text: And the spies saw a man come forth out of the city, and they said unto him, Shew us, we pray thee, the entrance into the city, and we will shew thee mercy.

modern.text: and when the spies saw a man coming out of the city, they said to him, “Please show us how to get into the city, and we will treat you kindly.”

original.text: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ הַשֹּׁ֣מְרִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ יוֹצֵ֣א מִן הָעִ֑יר וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ ל֗וֹ הַרְאֵ֤נוּ נָא֙ אֶת מְב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וְעָשִׂ֥ינוּ עִמְּךָ֖ חָֽסֶד

verses.restored: He showed them entrance of city, and they struck city by edge of sword; but the man and all his clan they sent away.

familiar.text: And when he shewed them the entrance into the city, they smote the city with the edge of the sword; but they let go the man and all his family.

modern.text: So the man showed them the entrance to the city, and they put the city to the sword but released that man and all his family.

original.text: וַיַּרְאֵם֙ אֶת מְב֣וֹא הָעִ֔יר וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת הָעִ֖יר לְפִי חָ֑רֶב וְאֶת הָאִ֥ישׁ וְאֶת כָּל מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֖וֹ שִׁלֵּֽחוּ

verses.restored: The man went to land of Hittites and built a city and called its name Luz; that is its name to this day.

familiar.text: And the man went into the land of the Hittites, and built a city, and called the name thereof Luz: which is the name thereof unto this day.

modern.text: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called it Luz, which is its name to this day. The Failure to Complete the Conquest

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ הָאִ֔ישׁ אֶ֖רֶץ הַחִתִּ֑ים וַיִּ֣בֶן עִ֗יר וַיִּקְרָ֤א שְׁמָהּ֙ ל֔וּז ה֣וּא שְׁמָ֔הּ עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean and its towns, Taanach and its towns, inhabitants of Dor and its towns, inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, or inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; Canaanite was determined to dwell in that land.

familiar.text: Neither did Manasseh drive out the inhabitants of Bethshean and her towns, nor Taanach and her towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and her towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and her towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and her towns: but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.

modern.text: At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and their villages; for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.

original.text: וְלֹא הוֹרִ֣ישׁ מְנַשֶּׁ֗ה אֶת בֵּית שְׁאָ֣ן וְאֶת בְּנוֹתֶיהָ֮ וְאֶת תַּעְנַ֣ךְ וְאֶת בְּנֹתֶיהָ֒ וְאֶת ישב ד֜וֹר וְאֶת בְּנוֹתֶ֗יהָ וְאֶת יוֹשְׁבֵ֤י יִבְלְעָם֙ וְאֶת בְּנֹתֶ֔יהָ וְאֶת יוֹשְׁבֵ֥י מְגִדּ֖וֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיּ֨וֹאֶל֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בָּאָ֥רֶץ הַזֹּֽאת

verses.restored: It was, when Israel grew strong, that they put Canaanite to forced labor, but they did not surely dispossess them.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Israel was strong, that they put the Canaanites to tribute, and did not utterly drive them out.

modern.text: When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּֽי חָזַ֣ק יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י לָמַ֑ס וְהוֹרֵ֖ישׁ לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: Ephraim did not dispossess Canaanite dwelling in Gezer; Canaanite dwelt in their midst in Gezer.

familiar.text: Neither did Ephraim drive out the Canaanites that dwelt in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwelt in Gezer among them.

modern.text: Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.

original.text: וְאֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ לֹ֣א הוֹרִ֔ישׁ אֶת הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י הַיּוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּגָ֑זֶר וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ בְּגָֽזֶר

verses.restored: Zebulun did not dispossess inhabitants of Kitron or inhabitants of Nahalol; Canaanite dwelt in their midst and became forced labor.

familiar.text: Neither did Zebulun drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites dwelt among them, and became tributaries.

modern.text: Zebulun failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; so the Canaanites lived among them and served as forced laborers.

original.text: זְבוּלֻ֗ן לֹ֤א הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י קִטְר֔וֹן וְאֶת יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י נַהֲלֹ֑ל וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ לָמַֽס

verses.restored: Asher did not dispossess inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.

familiar.text: Neither did Asher drive out the inhabitants of Accho, nor the inhabitants of Zidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob:

modern.text: Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.

original.text: אָשֵׁ֗ר לֹ֤א הוֹרִישׁ֙ אֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י עַכּ֔וֹ וְאֶת יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י צִיד֑וֹן וְאֶת אַחְלָ֤ב וְאֶת אַכְזִיב֙ וְאֶת חֶלְבָּ֔ה וְאֶת אֲפִ֖יק וְאֶת רְחֹֽב

verses.restored: Asherite dwelt in midst of Canaanite inhabitants of land, for they did not dispossess them.

familiar.text: But the Asherites dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land: for they did not drive them out.

modern.text: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ הָאָ֣שֵׁרִ֔י בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֖י לֹ֥א הוֹרִישֽׁוֹ

verses.restored: Naphtali did not dispossess inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or inhabitants of Beth-anath; he dwelt in midst of Canaanite inhabitants of land, and inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced labor for them.

familiar.text: Neither did Naphtali drive out the inhabitants of Bethshemesh, nor the inhabitants of Bethanath; but he dwelt among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land: nevertheless the inhabitants of Bethshemesh and of Bethanath became tributaries unto them.

modern.text: Naphtali failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath served them as forced laborers.

original.text: נַפְתָּלִ֗י לֹֽא הוֹרִ֞ישׁ אֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֤י בֵֽית שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ וְאֶת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י בֵית עֲנָ֔ת וַיֵּ֕שֶׁב בְּקֶ֥רֶב הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיֹשְׁבֵ֤י בֵֽית שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ֙ וּבֵ֣ית עֲנָ֔ת הָי֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם לָמַֽס

verses.restored: Amorite pressed children of Dan into hill country, for they did not allow them to come down to valley.

familiar.text: And the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the mountain: for they would not suffer them to come down to the valley:

modern.text: The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.

original.text: וַיִּלְחֲצ֧וּ הָאֱמֹרִ֛י אֶת בְּנֵי דָ֖ן הָהָ֑רָה כִּי לֹ֥א נְתָנ֖וֹ לָרֶ֥דֶת לָעֵֽמֶק

verses.restored: Amorite was determined to dwell at Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim; but hand of house of Joseph grew heavy, and they became forced labor.

familiar.text: But the Amorites would dwell in mount Heres in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim: yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became tributaries.

modern.text: And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.

original.text: וַיּ֤וֹאֶל הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת בְּהַר חֶ֔רֶס בְּאַיָּל֖וֹן וּבְשַֽׁעַלְבִ֑ים וַתִּכְבַּד֙ יַ֣ד בֵּית יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיִּהְי֖וּ לָמַֽס

verses.restored: Border of Amorite was from ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

familiar.text: And the coast of the Amorites was from the going up to Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.

modern.text: And the border of the Amorites extended from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.

original.text: וּגְבוּל֙ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י מִֽמַּעֲלֵ֖ה עַקְרַבִּ֑ים מֵהַסֶּ֖לַע וָמָֽעְלָה

translation_notes: Judges begins after Joshua by revisiting conquest as incomplete, contested, and locally negotiated rather than total and settled.

Adoni-bezek interprets his mutilation as measure-for-measure repayment for mutilations he committed. The text reports retaliatory disability-making and must not normalize torture, amputation, or revenge justice.
Jerusalem traditions in Judges 1 stand in tension with Joshua's allotment and ongoing Jebusite presence notices, requiring source and compositional audit.
Achsah's water request repeats Joshua 15 and again shows that land without springs is not viable inheritance; her agency must be preserved without romanticizing marriage-as-prize patriarchy.
The Kenite note preserves non-Israelite kinship presence through Moses' in-laws and should complicate ethnic-purity readings.
Iron-chariot notices, determined Canaanite presence, and repeated non-dispossession formulas dismantle any simple total-conquest reading.
Forced-labor notices appear across multiple tribes. Survival under tribute or labor is not justice or peaceful integration.
safety_note: Do not use Judges 1 to justify mutilation, conquest, ethnic domination, forced labor, treating women as rewards, or modern territorial claims. Center the chapter's admission of incomplete control, mixed populations, Achsah's resource demand, and the need to reject revenge and coerced labor as ethical models.
